text:
J.T. Miller's first full season as Rangers captain has been better than the scoresheet says. New York takes 61% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, almost 13 points better than when he sits. He keeps getting looks too: 4 goals on 7.2 expected, and none in his last five games on 3.0 expected.

The frustrating part is the finish around him. The Rangers have scored 10.4 fewer goals than their chances deserve with Miller out there, a gap that usually swings back. Evolving-Hockey saw the same pattern last season: his expected wins were well above his actual wins, the chances there and the finishing not.

That makes him one of the clearer "due" cases in the league. His ice time is up over the last ten games, he is still a setup man by Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, and our projection lands around 61 points. If you're judging the captaincy by goals in November, you're probably judging too early.
headline: Miller's chances deserve better than four goals
